thread:
Priya Rao: hey team — p95 for text-gen (gen-3) in us-west1 has been drifting up for ~7m, currently 320ms vs 200ms SLO. dashboards show sustained queuing at the GPU admission point.
Dan Wu: ugh. any spike in QPS or bigger payloads?
Priya Rao: no obvious QPS spike, avg tokens per request steady. but max_batch enforcement metric shows we're frequently hitting the max_pack_window and forcing small packing which increases headroom loss.
Alice Kim: can you paste the admission logs?
Priya Rao: sure. copied snippets: `ADMISSION allow=false reason=max_batch_reached pack_size=32 queue_length=74 p95_wait=120ms` and `PREFILL eviction=true kv_hits=0 eviction_count=12`
Marco Silva: that fits the pattern — continuous small requests filling KV/prefill windows and then we flip to single-request batches when max_batch gates kicks in. tail latency balloons.
SRE Oncall: infra metrics look normal for GPU util (60-70%). the admission controller is the choke. looks like packing fragmentation + the max_batch cap for the model flavor.
Dan Wu: any rolling deploys or recent config changes to admission thresholds?
Priya Rao: no deploys. did change default max_batch for gen-3 two weeks ago to 32 to save cost. wonder if regional traffic profile changed and that default hurts in us-west1.
Alice Kim: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase max_batch to 48 for us-west1 (risk: longer batching tail), 2) reduce max_batch to 16 so admission can favor more even packing (weird but sometimes reduces head-of-line waits), 3) force degrade to gen-2 for certain routes, 4) add admission backpressure by lowering concurrency per-GPU.
Marco Silva: increasing max_batch seems counterintuitive — if we hit max we create big batches but prefills + KV cause wasted cycles. reducing might allow more frequent packs, though each pack smaller. Either way we should avoid routing changes that cause extra cold-starts.
SRE Oncall: also seeing intermittent packet drops on the dataplane between adm service and gRPC pool (retries spike). could be contributing to observed SLO misses.
Dan Wu: ok test plan: run two experiments A/B in us-west1 on a small subset (10% traffic) — exp A: reduce max_batch to 16 + bump packing window to 30ms; exp B: fallback to gen-2 for lower-priority routes. compare p95 and token cost.
Priya Rao: I'll set the rollout. creating config change now. command: `./infractl apply --env us-west1 --service admission --set max_batch=16 --set pack_window_ms=30 --rollout 10% --note "emergency p95 mitigation"`
infra-bot: @Priya Rao started rollout 10% for admission (us-west1). change id: change-2026-07-23-01. monitors: #alerts/admission-p95, #dash/gen3-usw-p95.
Alice Kim: great. also open a short-lived alert to page if p95 > 250ms for more than 2m post-change.
SRE Oncall: spawned a debug collector to capture admission traces and gRPC retry logs for the next 15m.
Marco Silva: quick thought on root cause: we optimized default max_batch for cost when traffic was uniformly long-ish. If distribution shifted to many short requests (PLG adoption), the packing heuristics mis-estimate headroom and we oscillate into inefficient batching. need adaptive max_batch that considers recent payload length histogram.
Dan Wu: agreed. for medium-term, add a sliding-window estimator that adjusts max_batch per model per-region every minute. short-term we need data to prove hypothesis.
Priya Rao: rollout at 10% now. baseline p95 at rollout start: 318ms. will report after 5m.
(3m later)
Priya Rao: update: at 10% with max_batch=16, p95 for that slice down to 210ms. token cost +2%. overall us-west1 p95 improved by ~12%.
Dan Wu: nice. any signs of increased GPU overhead for same QPS?
Priya Rao: yes slight increase in tokens/sec per-GPU (+3%) but within threshold. no extra cold-starts.
Alice Kim: cool, can ramp to 50% and watch tail. recommended: keep gen-3 for critical routes but apply max_batch=16 for PLG routes.
Marco Silva: open follow-up: implement adaptive max_batch and a quick signal in the admission controller to detect packing fragmentation (low kv_hit_rate + high eviction_count) and shrink batch target proactively.
SRE Oncall: also filing a ticket to investigate dataplane retries — could be amplifying queueing. ticket: INFRA-4532.
Priya Rao: increasing rollout to 50%. infra-bot: confirmed.
infra-bot: rollout 50% complete. change-2026-07-23-01: 50% traffic.
(10m later)
Priya Rao: 50% slice p95 stable ~205ms, overall us-west1 p95 228ms. still above SLO but trending down.
Dan Wu: good. next steps: 1) finish rollout if stable, 2) schedule adaptive-max-batch spike, 3) estimate cost impact of keeping reduced max_batch by traffic class. Priya can you capture 1h of traces and cost delta?
Priya Rao: on it. I'll also add a small canary that routes new PLG tokens through an alternate admission queue to validate KV hit improvements.
Alice Kim: thanks everyone. will update the postmortem template with the actions and add a note for product about PLG traffic shape change. :memo:
Marco Silva: long-term: procurement/infra should consider regional capacity for short-request-heavy traffic — smaller instance types with lower-latency packing might be cheaper than trying to tune max_batch only.
SRE Oncall: closing loop for now, keeping alert noise muted until we decide on permanent config. page if p95 > 260ms.
Priya Rao: thanks — will follow up with tickets and timeline.
